When Do Covert Channels Emerge? Probing Steganographic Capacity in
Multimodal Agents via Diffusion VAEs Latents
Anonymous Authors1
Abstract
cally inspects the visible pixel content and any associated
metadata or captions to check for potential harm. What the
monitor may miss is that agents sharing the same pretrained
models also share a latent representation of each image, and
that representation can carry information not semantically
apparent from ordinary pixel-level inspection.
This paper investigates when diffusion VAE latents can
support covert communication under shared-model assump-
tions. A sender that can access a compatible VAE check-
point can embed a binary message into a cover image by
adding small signed perturbations to selected latent positions
before decoding. A receiver sharing the same checkpoint
and a coordination seed can re-encode the received image
and recover the message from the sign of those perturbations
relative to a clean baseline. The decoded image is visually
similar to the original; the information it carries is readable
only to an agent with access to the latent space.
Multi-agent AI systems increasingly communi-
cate through shared images, raising concerns
about covert communication channels that may
not be apparent from pixel-level monitors or hu-
man auditors. We study this risk using a training-
free construction that perturbs diffusion VAE
latents and tests whether the signal survives a
decode–reencode round trip. We structure this as
an adversarial evaluation, probing covert chan-
nel capacity under shared model assumptions,
and benchmarking monitoring regimes that re-
flect realistic monitor setups for multi-agent im-
age transmission. Across CIFAR-10, Caltech101,
and a 1,000-image ImageNet-family subset, and
across 3 VAE architectures, our perturbations are
reliably recoverable with > 97% bit accuracy at
ϵ = 2.0, and the channel survives realistic image
transformations at higher perturbation strengths.
We evaluate detectability under multiple monitor-
ing regimes, finding that detection performance
depends strongly on monitor capability, ranging
from near-chance for pixel-only monitors to near-
perfect for reference-aware detectors. These re-
sults suggest that covert communication in vision
models is a monitor-subversion threat relevant to
AI-control-style evaluations, and that evaluations
of multi-agent vision coordination should explic-
itly stress-test monitoring capability.
Rather than designing an optimized steganographic system,
we use a minimal construction as a probe to study when such
channels are viable. We design a suite of experiments to
characterize when this channel works, why it works, when
it breaks, and how a monitor can detect it. Our results move
beyond a simple proof-of-concept to provide an empirical
characterization of the channel across datasets, models, per-
turbation strengths, image transformations, and monitoring
regimes. A complementary directional gain analysis, how-
ever, shows that local VAE Jacobian geometry can serve
as a better selection criterion. On the monitoring side, we
find that detectability is not a fixed property of the channel
but depends sharply on what information the monitor can
access.
1. Introduction
Our contributions are:
Multi-agent scaffolds increasingly rely on images as a
shared communication medium. Agents exchange images
through browsers, shared workspaces, generated visualiza-
tions, screenshots, and perception pipelines. Within such
infrastructure, a human overseer or automated monitor typi-
1. We define a threat model for image-based covert
communication between multi-agent systems through
shared VAE representations, and situate it in the
broader landscape of adversarial steganography and
multi-agent collusion.

Under what conditions does a timing covert channel transmit data?

When deliberate delays between packets or events encode binary information

#### Learn More

Timing covert channels transmit data when participants introduce deliberate variations in the intervals between packets or events that correspond to specific binary values according to a prearranged encoding scheme. This approach succeeds because network timing jitter is a natural occurrence that security systems rarely analyze for intentional patterns amid legitimate traffic fluctuations. The underlying principle connects to information theory where modulation of inter-arrival times serves as a low-bandwidth but stealthy communication medium. Awareness of these conditions is vital for comprehending advanced persistent threats that leverage protocol timing to maintain command and control links. It also motivates the adoption of traffic shaping technologies that enforce consistent timing behaviors across network flows.

How is information concealed in IP packet headers for covert channels?

Through manipulation of identification TTL or flags fields

The underlying mechanism reflects how application layer protocols prioritize flexibility and backward compatibility over exhaustive validation of all possible content variations. Understanding these encoding locations is important because web traffic constitutes a large portion of modern network communications making it an attractive target for stealthy data transfers. Advanced defenses thus incorporate header analysis and anomaly detection tailored to common web protocol extensions.

When did formal analysis of covert channels begin?

In the early 1970s

#### Learn More

The emergence of formal analysis in the early 1970s coincided with the development of multilevel secure operating systems designed to handle classified information across different clearance levels. Researchers recognized that shared resources such as memory pages and processor caches could inadvertently serve as conduits for unauthorized information flow between isolated processes. This realization prompted the creation of analytical frameworks to model and mitigate such leaks, influencing subsequent standards in computer security and the design of reference monitors that enforce strict access controls.
Consequently, error-correcting codes or redundant signaling become necessary for covert communications to maintain integrity, highlighting why robust detection systems often focus on statistical deviations in inter-packet intervals.

What requirements must exist to create a covert channel?

Compromised sender and receiver plus shared unintended resource

#### Learn More

Establishing a covert channel fundamentally depends on the presence of a compromised endpoint that can manipulate a shared resource while another compromised party observes those manipulations. The shared resource must exhibit observable states that are not policed by the system's security mechanisms, allowing information to traverse isolation boundaries. This requirement underscores the importance of comprehensive system auditing and resource isolation techniques in preventing unintended communication paths in both operating systems and distributed networks.

What is the etymology of the term covert channel?

Covert refers to hidden while channel denotes a pathway for signals

#### Learn More

The terminology originates from combining the concept of concealment with the notion of a communication conduit, reflecting the hidden nature of these pathways within legitimate system operations. This linguistic construction emphasizes how such channels exploit the semantics of resource sharing rather than relying on overt protocol violations. Appreciating the etymological roots aids in distinguishing covert channels from traditional steganography by focusing attention on systemic properties instead of data embedding techniques.

How are covert channels classified within network security?

Primarily into storage channels and timing channels


Through encoding transmission via shared medium and subsequent decoding

#### Learn More

The establishment of a covert channel typically begins with the sender modulating data into an innocuous carrier signal through techniques like bit stuffing in protocol fields, followed by transmission across a common network pathway where the receiver extracts the original message via corresponding demodulation processes. This sequential workflow emerges from the need to maintain synchronization between communicating parties without alerting perimeter defenses that inspect for standard data transfer signatures. In theoretical models of secure systems, such procedures illustrate the limitations of mandatory access control policies that assume all communications occur through authorized and observable conduits. Recognizing the procedural intricacies involved fosters deeper insight into why comprehensive traffic analysis remains critical for mitigating unauthorized information flows in distributed computing environments.

Under what conditions will new covert channels emerge?

With added complexity in protocols and connected devices

#### Learn More

Increased intricacy in network protocols and device interconnections creates opportunities for unintended data transmission paths because designers prioritize functionality over exhaustive security validation during development phases. As systems incorporate more layers of abstraction and diverse hardware components, subtle interactions between these elements allow sophisticated actors to encode information within legitimate operations without triggering standard monitoring mechanisms. This phenomenon underscores the necessity for rigorous threat modeling in evolving infrastructures where the proliferation of interconnected technologies expands the attack surface in ways that traditional perimeter defenses cannot fully address.

What uncommon detail characterizes advanced covert channels?

Some achieve over one hundred bits per second in ideal settings

#### Learn More

Advanced implementations leverage optimized encoding schemes and minimal protocol overhead to transmit information at rates exceeding one hundred bits per second under controlled network conditions with low latency and high reliability. Such performance stems from careful selection of carrier signals that blend seamlessly with normal traffic patterns while maximizing information density per transmission unit. Understanding these capabilities highlights the evolving sophistication of information leakage techniques and the corresponding demand for high-resolution anomaly detection systems capable of operating at scale across enterprise environments.

Why is statistical analysis needed to detect covert channels?

Hidden signals appear as minor anomalies in large traffic volumes


They drove adoption of mandatory access controls and traffic normalization

#### Learn More

The recognition of covert channels prompted fundamental shifts toward mandatory access control models that enforce information flow policies based on security labels rather than discretionary permissions alone. Network architects responded by developing traffic normalizers that rewrite packets to remove potential encoding artifacts and ensure deterministic behavior across all transmissions. These developments reflect an ongoing evolution in security engineering where theoretical analyses of information leakage have translated into practical standards that influence both hardware and software implementations in critical systems.

Why does the IP time to live field enable covert channels?

Minor modifications carry data while preserving routing functionality

#### Learn More

In storage-based covert channels the receiving entity retrieves embedded information by monitoring designated locations where the sender has previously written data using shared system resources or memory structures accessible to both parties. 
Where does the receiver extract signals in a storage covert channel?

From predetermined shared attributes or memory locations

#### Learn More

Transmission Control Protocol User Datagram Protocol Domain Name System and Hypertext Transfer Protocol frequently serve as vehicles due to their ubiquity and the presence of extensible fields or timing characteristics that accommodate hidden payloads without immediate detection. These protocols operate at different layers of the network stack providing diverse opportunities for embedding data through header modifications sequence manipulations or payload padding strategies. The widespread adoption of these standards necessitates comprehensive monitoring solutions that account for protocol-specific behaviors to prevent systematic exploitation across both legacy and modern infrastructures.

How does acoustic signaling create nonnetwork covert channels?

By modulating sound emissions between nearby compromised systems

#### Learn More

Acoustic signaling establishes nonnetwork covert channels by exploiting the physical properties of sound waves generated from hardware components such as speakers, fans, or hard drives within compromised computing systems. 
What typical data rate do basic timing covert channels achieve?

One bit every several seconds

#### Learn More

Basic timing covert channels typically achieve data rates of approximately one bit every several seconds because they rely on modulating inter-event intervals or resource contention periods that must remain distinguishable from normal system variability measured in milliseconds or seconds. This limitation arises from the need to maintain synchronization between sender and receiver while avoiding detection thresholds established by statistical monitoring tools that analyze variance in timing distributions. The underlying mechanism involves encoding binary values through deliberate delays or accelerations in observable actions such as network packet transmissions or processor scheduling events. In the broader field of information leakage research, these rates contrast sharply with higher-bandwidth channels that exploit storage resources for faster transfers reaching hundreds of bits per second. Understanding these performance characteristics matters for risk assessment because even low-rate channels can exfiltrate small yet highly sensitive payloads like cryptographic keys over extended operational periods in targeted attacks.
#### Learn More

Adjusting the TCP window size creates an information channel because the field value directly influences flow control behavior and remains visible to any observer positioned along the network path between sender and receiver. Collaborating parties can agree upon a mapping that associates specific window values with particular data symbols thereby allowing the sender to encode messages through seemingly legitimate adjustments to transmission parameters. This technique leverages the protocol header fields that are essential for reliable data delivery yet are not protected against semantic manipulation by endpoints. Network security analysts must consider such protocol level channels when designing traffic analysis tools because they can operate at low bandwidth while remaining difficult to distinguish from natural variations caused by congestion or application behavior. Mitigating these risks often requires deep packet inspection combined with anomaly detection algorithms tuned to recognize unnatural patterns in header field distributions.
Ultimately these considerations drive ongoing research into zero trust architectures that minimize shared resources capable of serving as unintended communication media.

In what way can packet checksums hide information?

Intentional data tweaks produce checksums that represent secret bits

#### Learn More

Packet checksum fields can conceal information when an adversary intentionally modifies payload bits in a controlled manner that produces a resulting checksum value encoding the desired secret data. The receiver reconstructs the hidden message by examining the checksum rather than the original payload thereby allowing communication that appears consistent with normal protocol operation to external observers. This method exploits the deterministic nature of checksum calculations while relying on the fact that checksums are rarely inspected for semantic content beyond basic error detection. Security practitioners must account for such techniques when performing forensic analysis of captured traffic because they demonstrate how integrity mechanisms themselves can be repurposed for covert signaling. Developing countermeasures involves either encrypting checksum protected fields or implementing redundant verification procedures that detect anomalous modifications inconsistent with expected data patterns.

What physical network property enables timing covert channels?

Precise control and measurement of interpacket arrival intervals

#### Learn More

Precise control over inter packet arrival intervals enables timing covert channels because network interface hardware and operating system schedulers allow fine grained manipulation of transmission delays that can be measured accurately by a remote observer. Collaborating entities establish a clock reference and encode information through deliberate variations in gap durations between successive packets sent over a shared medium. This approach capitalizes on the high resolution timing capabilities present in modern network stacks while avoiding direct modification of packet contents that might trigger integrity checks. Detection of such channels demands specialized monitoring equipment capable of capturing microsecond level variations and applying statistical analysis to identify deviations from Poisson or self similar traffic models. The existence of these physical layer opportunities highlights the need for comprehensive threat modeling that includes hardware and protocol timing characteristics in secure system design.

How does temperature modulation enable covert channels?

Heat variations between components signal data in air gapped setups

#### Learn More

Temperature modulation establishes covert channels in air gapped environments by allowing one compromised component to generate controlled heat patterns that propagate through physical structures and are sensed by thermal sensors on another isolated device. The sender encodes binary data through sequences of processor intensive operations that raise local temperatures while the receiver decodes messages by monitoring corresponding fluctuations in its own thermal readings. This physical side channel exploits fundamental thermodynamic properties and the thermal coupling that exists between adjacent hardware elements even when no electrical or network connections are present. Researchers have demonstrated practical implementations achieving low but detectable data rates sufficient for exfiltrating small cryptographic keys or status information. Consequently investment in covert channel detection capabilities represents a critical component of comprehensive risk management strategies for technology intensive industries.

Which real world incidents involved suspected covert channels?

State sponsored cyber operations targeting sensitive networks

#### Learn More

State sponsored operations have repeatedly leveraged covert channels to extract intelligence from air gapped networks and high security enclaves where conventional remote access methods would be detected by monitoring systems. These incidents typically involve sophisticated malware capable of modulating hardware signals or protocol fields to communicate with external receivers positioned near the target facility. Attribution efforts often rely on forensic examination of timing patterns packet header anomalies and thermal signatures that match known techniques developed by advanced persistent threat groups. Such real world cases illustrate the transition of academic covert channel research into operational cyber warfare tools employed against critical infrastructure and defense contractors. Studying these events provides valuable lessons for improving detection algorithms and hardening systems against nation state level adversaries who possess both the resources and motivation to exploit subtle information leakage paths.

How does a receiver interpret timing covert channel signals?

By mapping measured delays or intervals back to original bits

#### Learn More

In timing covert channels the receiver relies on precise measurement of inter-event delays to reconstruct encoded information because the sender deliberately varies the timing of shared resource accesses or network packets according to a mutually agreed protocol that assigns specific intervals to logical bits or symbols. Accurate interpretation therefore demands synchronized high-resolution timers and statistical filtering to separate intentional modulations from background system noise or scheduling jitter. This decoding mechanism exposes fundamental limitations in systems that expose observable timing side effects without sufficient randomization or access controls, enabling stealthy information transfer that bypasses conventional data-flow policies. Understanding such receiver behavior is essential for designing robust defenses that either obscure timing signals or enforce strict isolation between potential sender and receiver entities.

What inputs does the sender of a covert channel require?

Secret message plus agreed encoding scheme with the receiver

#### Learn More

A covert channel sender must possess both the confidential payload intended for exfiltration and a shared encoding convention that maps data elements onto observable system behaviors such as resource contention patterns or packet inter-arrival times. Without prior agreement on this encoding scheme the receiver cannot reliably distinguish meaningful signals from random fluctuations, rendering the channel ineffective. The requirement for coordinated knowledge underscores why covert channels typically arise only between colluding processes or users who have established a communication protocol in advance. This dependency also explains the importance of key distribution and synchronization mechanisms in maintaining channel fidelity across noisy environments.

Why does network congestion disrupt covert channels?

Unpredictable delays distort timing signals and increase error rates

#### Learn More

Network congestion introduces variable queuing delays and packet loss that superimpose unpredictable jitter onto the carefully crafted timing intervals used by covert channels, thereby distorting the original signal and elevating bit error rates at the receiver. #### Learn More

Current research into covert channels within encrypted flows emphasizes behavioral analysis and anomaly detection techniques that operate without requiring decryption of the protected content. Researchers examine metadata features including packet sizes, inter-arrival times, and flow volumes to identify deviations from expected protocol behaviors that may indicate hidden information streams. These methods leverage machine learning models trained on legitimate traffic patterns to flag subtle inconsistencies introduced by covert embedding processes. Such approaches matter because they preserve privacy during inspection while addressing the growing prevalence of encrypted traffic that traditional payload analysis can no longer access directly.

Under what conditions do covert channels pose the highest threat?

When sender holds classified data and receiver sits outside perimeter

#### Learn More

Covert channels present the highest threat levels when a sender possessing classified or sensitive data maintains communication with an external receiver positioned beyond organizational security perimeters.

What distinguishes synchronous covert channels?

Requirement for tight clock alignment between sender and receiver

#### Learn More

Synchronous covert channels depend on precise clock synchronization between communicating parties to ensure that timing based signals are correctly interpreted without ambiguity or loss of information. This requirement emerges because the encoding relies on specific intervals or phases of activity that must align perfectly for the receiver to distinguish intended patterns from background noise or unrelated system events. The underlying mechanism involves coordinated modulation of resource usage or packet transmission times which demands shared temporal references often achieved through external clocks or protocol based synchronization methods. In broader security contexts this characteristic makes synchronous channels more susceptible to disruption by network jitter or processor scheduling variations compared to asynchronous alternatives. Analysis of these requirements informs the development of robust detection systems that monitor for anomalous timing correlations across isolated domains.

How does an asynchronous covert channel operate?

Without precise timing coordination making it more robust

#### Learn More

An asynchronous covert channel transmits hidden information by modulating data flows through variable intervals and irregular patterns rather than depending on synchronized clocks between communicating parties. This operational mode exploits the natural jitter and latency variations present in packet-switched networks, enabling the receiver to interpret signals based on relative timing differences or statistical distributions instead of absolute synchronization points. Such channels demonstrate greater resilience because disruptions like congestion or route changes affect timing references less critically than in coordinated systems, thereby allowing persistent leakage of sensitive information across security boundaries. The underlying principle connects to broader network security concepts where protocol flexibility inadvertently creates opportunities for information exfiltration that evade timing-based intrusion detection systems.

Why are asynchronous designs often chosen for covert channels?

Greater tolerance to network variability and jitter

#### Learn More

Asynchronous covert channel designs are frequently selected because they accommodate fluctuations in network conditions without requiring continuous alignment of sender and receiver clocks. Network variability and jitter arise from routing dynamics, queuing delays, and traffic congestion, which can desynchronize tightly timed communications and cause data loss in synchronous alternatives. By relying on observable statistical anomalies or sequence-based encodings, these channels maintain functionality across heterogeneous environments such as the internet where precise timing guarantees do not exist. This choice underscores a fundamental trade-off in covert communication engineering between transmission reliability and the risk of detection through enforced synchronization protocols.

What current research targets covert channels in encrypted flows?

Behavioral analysis and anomaly detection without decryption

#### Learn More

Current research into covert channels within encrypted flows emphasizes behavioral analysis and anomaly detection techniques that operate without requiring decryption of the protected content. Researchers examine metadata features including packet sizes, inter-arrival times, and flow volumes to identify deviations from expected protocol behaviors that may indicate hidden information streams. These methods leverage machine learning models trained on legitimate traffic patterns to flag subtle inconsistencies introduced by covert embedding processes. Such approaches matter because they preserve privacy during inspection while addressing the growing prevalence of encrypted traffic that traditional payload analysis can no longer access directly.

Under what conditions do covert channels pose the highest threat?

When sender holds classified data and receiver sits outside perimeter

#### Learn More

High security networks demand scrutiny of covert storage channels because shared memory regions and file system objects can inadvertently permit data transfer across different classification levels despite enforced access controls. These channels arise when processes at varying security clearances utilize common storage mechanisms without sufficient sanitization or isolation barriers in place. Addressing this requirement involves implementing rigorous auditing and mandatory access policies that account for both direct and indirect communication vectors. Such analyses form a cornerstone of multilevel security architectures where even minimal leakage could compromise national security interests.

In what way does packet padding create covert channels?

Filling unused bytes with encoded patterns observable by the receiver

#### Learn More

Packet padding in network protocols creates covert channels by allowing unused byte positions to be populated with encoded information that the intended receiver can extract while appearing as random filler to observers.
